claim: The Commission's transition timeline for legacy devices and for Regulation devices placed on the market before mandatory use (an undated one-page Commission document linked from the EUDAMED overview page) gives 28 November 2026 as the "Deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module", after the notice published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, mandatory use of the UDI/Dev module from 28 May 2026 and a 6-month transition period. limitations: The Commission timeline is a one-page document with no document date, no version and no legal citation, and the overview page that links it prints no November 2026 date; the date is as the Commission document labels it, read on 16 November 2026. Decision (EU) 2025/2371 states no calendar date (read on EUR-Lex through a text-extraction tool; a second look at the Official Journal PDF is advisable before the date is cited in a client deliverable).

Friday 27 November 2026 is a ClinicOps planning date, not a regulatory date: 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, and calendar-month counting from the 27 November 2025 publication can give 27 November 2026. ClinicOps has not established which count controls, and the earlier commentary that gave 27 November as the date is not used as a source.

Article 123(3)(e) MDR as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 refers to "no later than 12 months from the date of publication of the notice referred to in Article 34(3)" for the entry of Article 29 information for the devices listed in (e)(i) and (ii); counted from 27 November 2025 that points to 27 November 2026. This is ClinicOps' reading of the consolidated text and has not had a legal read; whether the Commission timeline's 28 November 2026 and Article 123(3)(e) describe the same obligation is not established. The Commission's undated Q&A cites Article 123(3)(d), but the consolidated text places the 12-month rule in (e) and the 6-month application rule in (d).
Rewritten 16 November 2026 to reconcile this claim with CO-CLM-0020 (shared fact_key and value). After 28 November 2026 the wording must move to the past tense.
Whether a specific device qualifies as a legacy device is a manufacturer determination.

source_date: Commission legacy-device transition timeline (undated); notice published in the OJ on 27 November 2025
not_established: The legal basis or counting rule behind the date: the Commission timeline cites none and the Decision states no calendar date.
Whether a particular device counts as a legacy device.
ics_summary: EUDAMED: Commission deadline to register legacy devices in the UDI/Devices module
ics_note: ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.

claim: Under Article 22 MDR, a person who places a system or procedure pack on the market under Article 22(1) or (3) is not thereby the manufacturer of the constituent devices, whereas under Article 22(4) a combination outside 22(1) and (3) is treated as a device in its own right and that person assumes the obligations of a manufacturer; Article 32 places the SS(C)P duty on the manufacturer, so on ClinicOps' reading no SS(C)P duty arises for a pack registered under Article 22(1) or (3).
limitations: The Article 22 and Article 32 text is primary; the conclusion that no SS(C)P duty arises for the pack is ClinicOps reasoning, not a stated Commission or MDCG position.
Constituent devices keep their own manufacturers' obligations, including any Article 32 duty.

Re-read on 16 November 2026 (EUR-Lex consolidated text of 10 January 2025, text-extraction tool). Article 22(4) is confirmed as read; the extraction of Article 22(1) did not show an express statement that the person is not the manufacturer of the constituent devices, which stays ClinicOps reading, as labelled above.
label: MDR Arts. 22 and 32: SS(C)P duty and system or procedure packs
not_established: Any Commission or MDCG statement that no SS(C)P duty arises for a pack.

claim: The EUDAMED system/procedure-pack registration records the highest risk class among the devices that form part of the pack, so a class III value on a PR-role record is inherited from a constituent device rather than being an ordinary classification of the pack itself; separately, MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 describes an SS(C)P document-control model in which an updated revision can exist while notified-body validation timing is in process, so a published revision may legitimately be published between validation cycles.
limitations: Sourced from the Commission EUDAMED Information Centre and non-binding MDCG guidance; do not convert a document-vs-record difference into an irregularity without establishing the exact process state.
Do not describe a system/procedure pack as itself a class III device on the strength of the inherited field.

label: Pack risk class is inherited; SS(C)P revisions between validations
source_date: EUDAMED help v2.27.0 (24 July 2026); MDCG 2019-9 rev.1 (March 2022)
not_established: That a difference between a document and a record is an irregularity.

claim: Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371 of 26 November 2025, published in the Official Journal on 27 November 2025, confirms four EUDAMED systems as functional: actor registration, UDI database and device registration, notified bodies and certificates, and market surveillance. It enters into force on the day of its publication and states no calendar date for mandatory use. The Commission's EUDAMED overview page states that this publication triggered a transition period of 6 months and that, as of 28 May 2026, these four modules became mandatory to use. For legacy devices the Commission's transition timeline gives 28 November 2026 as the deadline to register the device in the UDI/Dev module (see CO-CLM-0013); 28 November 2026 is a Saturday, so ClinicOps plans to finish by Friday 27 November 2026.
limitations: Read on 16 November 2026: the Commission EUDAMED overview page, the Commission legacy-device transition timeline PDF and the Decision on EUR-Lex (Articles 1 and 2 and recitals 3 to 6) through a text-extraction tool; a second look at the Official Journal PDF is advisable before any date is cited in a client deliverable.

The Decision states no calendar date; 28 May 2026 and 28 November 2026 come from Commission documents that carry no document date. The Commission's undated Q&A on the gradual roll-out cites Article 123(3)(d) MDR as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 (the consolidated text places the 12-month rule in 123(3)(e); see CO-CLM-0013) and says registration of legacy devices must be done "within 12 months from the publication in the OJEU", but states it has not been formally endorsed by the Commission, so it is not used as a source for a date.
Friday 27 November 2026 is a ClinicOps planning date, not a regulatory date. Whether a specific device is in scope is a manufacturer determination.
The vigilance and clinical-investigation modules are not among the four modules (see CO-CLM-0050). Certificate registration has its own later date in the Commission timeline and is not covered here.
Rewritten 16 November 2026: the earlier text gave 27 or 28 November from commentary and described a 12-month period taken from commentary; both are replaced by what the Commission documents state.
label: Decision (EU) 2025/2371: four EUDAMED modules functional and mandatory
source_date: Decision of 26 November 2025, OJ of 27 November 2025; Commission EUDAMED overview page (undated)
not_established: A calendar date in the Decision itself: the 28 May 2026 date comes from the Commission overview page.
Whether a particular device is in scope.

claim: Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Articles 5 to 8, for an initial clinical trial application: validation takes 10 days (up to 25 with a request for information); the Part I assessment takes 45 days from the validation date in steps of 26, 12 and 7 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information and by up to 50 days for expert consultation on advanced-therapy and Annex point 1 products; Part II takes 45 days, extended by up to 31 days for a request for information; the decision follows within 5 days of the later of the Part I reporting date and the end of Part II. The EMA CTIS Sponsor Handbook states 60 days without and 106 days with requests for information, and describes a pause of all timers from 22 December to 8 January.
limitations: Read from the Official Journal text (Publications Office) as consolidated to 5 December 2022; later amendments were not checked. The winter pause is an EMA/CTCG practice described in the Sponsor Handbook, not in the Regulation, and the 2026-27 dates rest on its generic wording. Weekend and holiday roll-forward follows the handbook and Regulation 1182/71 Article 3; holiday calendars belong to the Member State and are not built in. Where a request for information falls inside an assessment is not fixed by the Regulation, so the tool places it at the end of the assessment it extends. The 156-day advanced-therapy maximum is ClinicOps arithmetic, not a stated figure. Planning aid, not legal advice.
label: CTR Arts. 5-8: initial application periods in CTIS
source_date: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 as consolidated to 5 December 2022 (OJ); EMA CTIS Sponsor Handbook section 3.1 (7 July 2026)
not_established: Amendments after 5 December 2022.
Member State public holidays.

claim: Under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 a manufacturer outside the Union may place a device on the Union market only if it designates a sole authorised representative (Article 11(1)); the designation is valid only when accepted in writing (Article 11(2)); the representative's mandate includes verifying that the declaration of conformity and technical documentation have been drawn up and meeting the Article 31 registration obligations (Article 11(3)). Before placing a device other than a custom-made device on the market, manufacturers, authorised representatives and importers submit their identification information to the electronic system (Article 31(1)); the competent authority verifies it and obtains the single registration number (Article 31(2)). Importers verify that the device is registered (Article 13(4)).
limitations: Read from the consolidated text of 10 January 2025 on EUR-Lex on 16 November 2026 (passages located and summarised, not read in full); later consolidations were not checked. The text does not expressly make issue of the SRN a precondition for placing on the market, only submission before it. The list is a selection, not the full set of obligations of manufacturers, authorised representatives or importers. Orientation, not legal advice.
label: MDR Arts. 11, 13 and 31: authorised representative and registration
not_established: Later consolidations were not checked.
The list is a selection, not every obligation.

Read through a text-extraction tool; a second look at the live page is advisable before a client deliverable.
label: EUDAMED clinical investigation and vigilance modules: not yet mandatory

claim: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466 of 22 July 2025, published in the Official Journal on 23 July 2025, amends Implementing Regulation (EU) No 520/2012 and applies from 12 February 2026. Article 6(3) of Regulation 520/2012 as amended requires a marketing authorisation holder's pharmacovigilance subcontract to contain a clear description of the roles and responsibilities of the third parties; their obligation to exchange safety data with the holder, and the method of exchange if relevant; arrangements for inspection and auditing of the third parties; and their agreement to be audited by or on behalf of the holder and inspected by competent authorities. Article 6(4) bars onward subcontracting of assigned tasks without the holder's written consent. Article 13(1a) provides that a third party subcontracted for pharmacovigilance tasks shall be audited by or on behalf of the holder, taking into account the risk of the subcontracted activity.
limitations: Read on 16 November 2026 in the Official Journal act text on EUR-Lex through a text-extraction tool; the consolidated Regulation (EU) No 520/2012, Directive 2001/83/EC and GVP were not read for this claim, and a second look at the act is advisable before it is cited in a client deliverable.
The claim covers the clause set and audit provision only; the severity bands and GVP expectations in the SDEA checker are not covered. Planning aid, not legal advice.
label: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1466: clauses of a pharmacovigilance subcontract
source_date: Implementing Regulation of 22 July 2025, OJ of 23 July 2025; applies from 12 February 2026
not_established: The consolidated Regulation 520/2012, Directive 2001/83/EC and GVP were not read.
Whether a given agreement is adequate.

Any DHPC volume or timeline.

claim: Annex VII point 1.2 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 sets independence and impartiality requirements for notified bodies. Point 1.2.3 provides that the body, its top management and its assessment staff may not offer or provide consultancy services to the manufacturer (or to a commercial competitor) as regards the devices or processes under assessment. Point 1.2.4 provides that personnel formerly employed by a specific client, or who provided consultancy on devices to that client, may not be assigned to conformity assessment activities for that client (and its group) for a period of three years.
limitations: Read on 16 November 2026 in two places: the EUR-Lex consolidated text of 10 January 2025 and the legislation.gov.uk copy of the adopted text. Both reads went through a page summariser that limits verbatim quotation, so the points were located and summarised, not read as a continuous passage; they agree on the sub-point numbers and on the three-year period. Re-read points 1.2.3 and 1.2.4 in the Official Journal text before any wording that quotes them. The text does not say from which date the three years run. These are obligations of notified bodies, not of consultants: ClinicOps uses the three-year period as its own look-back for declarations by itself and by specialists, and does not claim that the Regulation imposes that check on partners. Later consolidations were not checked. Orientation, not legal advice.
label: MDR Annex VII 1.2: notified-body independence (consultancy and three-year look-back)
not_established: The date from which the three years run.
That the Regulation imposes a look-back check on consultants or partners.

claim: On load, no page listed in the ClinicOps sitemap requests anything from another origin, receives a Set-Cookie header, or writes to cookies, localStorage or sessionStorage. An automated browser test checks this in CI before each deployment. In the scripted Regulatory Integrity Scanner, Change Surface Mapper and Readiness Score journeys, only two kinds of data are written to browser storage: Scanner mapping profiles in localStorage, and the short hand-off to the assessment page in sessionStorage, which that page removes as it reads it.

The local CI run cannot see GitHub Pages' own response headers or server logs; the weekly production run of the same test sees the headers, and GitHub's connection logs are described in the privacy notice.

The meta Content-Security-Policy (connect-src 'none') blocks script network connections but does not stop a link click or a script that changes the page location, so it is defence in depth, not proof that nothing can leave.
Registered under id 0090 on 16 November 2026 to avoid collisions with parallel work; renumber if the main session prefers a contiguous sequence.
label: Sitemap pages: no third-party requests, cookies or non-listed browser storage writes
source_date: ClinicOps CI run of e2e/release_privacy_test.mjs, 16 November 2026
not_established: Behaviour in other browsers, with extensions, or on GitHub Pages response headers (checked only by the weekly production run).
That nothing can leave through a link click or navigation.

The list includes that the Danish translation is a faithful translation of the original text, that the choice of words and use of terminology is consistent, and that summaries of product characteristics, package leaflets and labelling are in correct Danish.

The page states the Agency's expectation of the text it proofreads; it does not state a legal obligation or a sanction. EMA's own expectations on medical terminology expertise were not read.

That the expectation applies to medical devices, clinical-trial material or national procedures.

claim: The EMA Guideline on computerised systems and electronic data in clinical trials (EMA, 2023) states, in its annex on agreements, that clear written agreements should be in place and signed by all involved parties and that responsibility for data integrity, security and confidentiality remains with the sponsor or the institution. It states that file and data transfers needed during the conduct of a trial should be pre-specified and the transfer process validated. In its annex on change control it states that requests for change should be documented and authorised, that the risk assessment should cover data integrity, current functionalities and regulatory compliance, that the system should be version controlled, and that investigators should be clearly informed of changes to forms such as eCRF or eCOA pages. It states that a dated and certified copy of the database and data should be archived and available on request.
